subject: Edge-region routing lapse — confirm impacted window & remediation options
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@fastshop.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-03-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: High checkout errors 07:42–07:58 UTC — need confirmation of impacted window

Evelyn / team,

We saw a spike of 502/503 errors affecting ~22% of checkout traffic between 07:42 and 07:58 UTC this morning (2029-03-01). The failures are correlated with requests routed to your edge in us-west-2; our infra fell back to local validation, which caused higher latency and dropped conversions.

Can you confirm whether this was an internal routing lapse on Redwood's side and whether it aligns with any scheduled changes? FastShop will likely request a remediation credit if this falls within the SLA exclusion threshold. I attached a quick screenshot of the customer-facing error rates and a short trace sample.

Attachments: slo-window-screenshot.png (image), minimal-trace.txt (text)

Requesting:
- confirmation of affected window in Redwood logs
- provisional statement re: SLA eligibility
- timeline for a postmortem / RCA

Thanks,
Samir Patel
SRE Lead, FastShop
samir@fastshop.com

Hi Samir — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot. We're looking into this immediately.

Quick asks while we triage:
- Can you attach a bundle with a few full traces (trace IDs and timestamps) covering 07:30–08:05 UTC? That will make our correlation much faster.
- Please confirm whether the error blowups were observed from multiple regions or concentrated on specific customer segments (we've seen partial-route symptoms before).

I’m looping in Marcus (runtime) and Naomi (incidents) to pull raw routing telemetry and the edge control-plane timeline. We'll aim to provide a verified impacted window within 3 business hours.

I note FastShop account FS-2387; I'll also flag this for expedited SLA adjudication once we validate the window.

Proposed 30-min call if needed: 12:00 or 15:00 PDT today — let me know which works.

Evelyn Hart

Subject: Re: High checkout errors 07:42–07:58 UTC — need confirmation of impacted window

Samir / team,

Preliminary notes from runtime telemetry: between 07:40:10–07:59:02 UTC we observed a partial-route policy mismatch in us-west-2 that routed ~19% of traffic to a legacy model-variant behind an older kernel. Those connections experienced elevated latencies which, combined with our prefix-cache coldstart under that variant, produced 502/503s for a subset of requests.

I have pulled the edge routing table changes and control-plane events — there was an automated streak of route refreshes at 07:39:58 UTC that coincides with the start of the errors. I'm attaching a short CSV extract (routing-events-uw2.csv) in the workspace.

At a high level: this looks like an internal routing/control-plane regression rather than customer misconfiguration. SLA eligibility will depend on exact overlapping timestamps once we correlate your traces to our ingress logs. If overlapping, the incident looks like it could qualify under Section 4.2 (Availability SLO, regional) for pro-rata relief.

What I need from FastShop: canonical trace IDs and a couple of example customer request IDs so I can join to ingress events.

-Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@fastshop.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-03-02T07:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High checkout errors 07:42–07:58 UTC — need confirmation of impacted window

Hi Samir — thanks for the bundle and the quick turnaround. I've completed a correlation pass across ingress logs, control-plane events, and your traces. Findings (summary):

- Verified overlapped window: 2029-03-01 07:42:07 UTC — 2029-03-01 07:58:59 UTC (matches your observed failures).
- Root cause signal: automated route refresh pushed a partial route (stale model-variant) to a subset of edge nodes; those nodes triggered prefix-cache coldstarts which increased head latency and created transient 502/503 responses.
- Impact: ~18–22% of checkout traffic in us-west-2 experienced elevated error rates and latency for that window.

Next steps and remedial items we will execute:
1) Full RCA (including the control-plane change that allowed the stale route) — deliverable in 5 business days.
2) Raw telemetry and a trace-join package — attached (trace_join_manifest.csv).
3) Provisional remedy: we will reserve a provisional credit bucket equivalent to 10% of the monthly usage for the affected routes for FS-2387 pending final adjudication. If final adjudication confirms a breach under SLA Section 4.2, we will apply the pro-rata credit per contract terms; if not confirmed, the provisional hold will be released.

We want to be transparent: the provisional credit is our interim gesture to reduce procurement friction — the final amount will follow the SLA math once timelines and sustained impact are validated.

Please confirm whether FastShop would like us to proceed with a joint RCA call tomorrow (2029-03-03) at 09:00 PDT or 11:00 PDT. I suggest 30–45 minutes.

Attachments: trace_join_manifest.csv

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Incident Response | Redwood Inference
